summary: Deschutes NF summit lookout: frame cabin built 1925, L-4 cab in the 1930s, closed and dismantled by 1953; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Frame cabin built 1925; replaced in the 1930s by an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Closed and dismantled by 1953; the register says the L-4 cab is now gone; no source describes what remains on the summit

access.note: The Black Crater Trailhead is day use only. The trail enters the Three Sisters Wilderness shortly after the trailhead, and wilderness permits are required. No source says whether the old lookout site itself is open.

visit.trail_note: Black Crater Trail #4058 starts at a Forest Service trailhead that is day use only, with a wilderness permit required

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 7,251 ft for the site, while a 1936 Forest Service station description gives 7,260 ft for the lookout house on the summit. The sources do not reconcile these; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Design is not in the current record (design null); the register and firelookout.com both support the 1925 frame cabin and the 1930s L-4 cab, so it is proposed as a fact, not a correction. The 1930s replacement has no exact year. Elevation differs (7,251 ft register vs 7,260 ft 1936 USFS station description) and is reported both ways. Current site condition is unknown: no source describes remains or public access to the old site. Search results included a 2026 real-estate blog and an AllTrails listing that describe the summit as burned in the 2003 B&B Fire; not used because they are not reliable sources about the lookout, but worth checking against Forest Service fire history. A Forest Service trail page sentence about a former lookout did not appear in the cached fetch, so it is not cited. Verification 2026-10-09: the story no longer calls the 1925 house the first house. A Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts, dated August 20, 1925, already refers to 'the Black Crater lookout house' (ice on its west side, reported by Blanchard), so the sources do not show when the summit house was first occupied; the September 1925 item describes a standard lookout house under construction.
